content.text: {"claims": [{"claim": 1, "text": "Remaining useful life prediction using recurrent neural networks with long short-term memory achieves 14.3% mean absolute percentage error on bearing run-to-failure sequences at the 50% consumed-life mark with 20 or more training sequences, and simple linear scaling of the health index by rated load and speed partially recovers cross-condition accuracy from 22-28% to 17.1%.", "sources": [{"id": "SYN-PUB-00593", "field": "abstract", "quote": "With 20 or more training sequences, mean absolute percentage error in RUL prediction stabilised near 14.3% at the 50% consumed-life mark."}, {"id": "SYN-PUB-00593", "field": "abstract", "quote": "Cross-condition generalisation degraded performance to 22–28% MAPE when the training and test operating conditions differed, but a simple linear scaling of the health index by rated load and speed partially recovered accuracy to 17.1%."}]}]}
